text:
mira: sketching a new synthetic generator shape — 'gated_sawtooth' — to repro the kernel-selection tail regression we saw on the servicing cluster. idea is QPS ramp -> sustained window -> gated drop to zero, repeat. want to stress kernel heuristics + kv cache churn.

alex: can you paste the generator config? need seq len distro, qps schedule, and kv warmup semantics.

mira: sure, prototype config below (yaml):
```yaml
generator: gated_sawtooth
qps: - ramp_start: 10
  ramp_end: 200
  ramp_seconds: 45
  sustain_seconds: 60
  gate_off_seconds: 20
sequence_length: {p50: 32, p90: 128, p99: 512}
kv_warmup: {requests: 5000, parallel: 32}
seed: 12345
record_trace: true
```

sam: nit: for apples-to-apples comparisons we must freeze:
- batcher/timer settings (batch_max_wait_ms, max_batch_size)
- kernel build flags / quantization profile
- deterministic seed and same replay input order
Also run both cold-kv and warm-kv variants.

ollie: add tracepoints and counters: `kernel_choice`, `batch_size_hist`, `kv_hit_rate`, `kv_latency_ms`. If possible emit per-request kernel metadata so we can correlate tail spikes to kernel selection.

infra-bot: test-run 1931112240: gated_sawtooth v1 executed against staging-cluster-3. Summary: 95th latency +12% vs baseline-run-1931109000, batch modal size shifted 1->2 during surge, kernel fallback seen during gate transitions. Raw logs: https://internal/logs/1931112240 (perm limited).

mira: thanks. plan: 1) add deterministic seed and replay harness wrapper; 2) ensure kv-warmup phase is explicit; 3) capture pprof + tracepoints during run; 4) run cold vs warm kv and attach diffs. I'll open a PR with the harness changes.

alex: :thumbsup: also try a microburst subphase (2x qps for 30s) inside the sustain window — that tends to expose batching timer interactions and kernel selection thrash.

sam: running a two-run compare now (baseline vs gated_sawtooth+kvwarm). will post numbers.

infra-bot: perf-diff 1931112260 attached: baseline->candidate 95th: 120ms -> 137ms, p99: 210ms -> 249ms; batch_size modal: 1 -> 2; kernel chosen changed from `kernel_v2` -> `kernel_v3` under surge.

mira: interesting — evidence points at kernel_v3 choosing a path that disables prefetch + different memory layout, which increases per-token latency when kv misses spike. hypothesis: kernel fallback on surge increases KV miss pressure, evicting hot prefixes.

ollie: next steps: instrument kernel selection hotpath with lightweight counters, add eviction / kv occupancy metrics, and collect per-token latency histograms (not just request-level).

mira: agreed. i'll add the counters to the runtime, update the harness to include microburst subphase, and attach replay artifacts. will post PR and a reproducible test matrix. thanks all :rocket:

alex: :eyes: ping me when the PR is up, i'll run a longer-duration replay (6h) overnight to catch rare tails.

sam: will also try toggling `batch_max_wait_ms` to see sensitivity.

mira: done for now, wrapping into issue #INF-927 and PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/inf/PR/6789 (draft).
